new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Muinane has an empty rule and there are no existing stress statements; this work supplies the typological fact that Muinane is a two-tone language with no stress described. Opened via the Internet Archive copy (2024-08-28) of SIL's current archive PDF; the listed open_url (SIL Colombia abstract.asp?id=12605) is a 404 and its 2007 archived catalogue page shows no online file at that time.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The grammar contains no phonology chapter (it defers to the 1967/1972 phonemic statement) and never mentions stress or accent; its only suprasegmental statement is that Muinane has two phonemic tones, high (acute) and low (unmarked), a two-tone system also exploited by the drum-signalling described in §I.D.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the full 87-page scanned has no hit for acento/acentuación/intensidad; 'tono' occurs only in the drum passage (pp. 7-8) and the p. 84 note. Section III.E 'La morfofonémica' (pp. 62-66) treats vowel elision and harmony only.
new_statements.identity_note: All works describe the same variety: the Muinane of La Sabana at the headwaters of the Cahuinarí (Amazonas, Colombia), data collected by the Waltons 1964-1980, principal informant Andrés Hernández Pakky of the Nejegaimɨjo clan; the 1967 chapter calls Muinane one of three mutually unintelligible 'dialects' of Bora (Bora, Miraña, Muinane), the later works treat it as a separate Boran language. The 1975 grammar notes only minor clan-level dialect differences. The Rosetta Project excerpt (archive.org rosettaproject_bmr_phon-1) is the 1972 Spanish translation 'Fonemas del muinane' of the 1967 chapter and breaks off at the start of the tone section.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no rule for Muinane; the 1967 phonemic statement (the standard phonology source, which the 1975 grammar and 2000 sketch both cite) establishes a two-tone system with no stress. The listed hdl (MPI PuRe item_406275) resolves to a bot-protected page whose PDF component is audience-restricted (not reachable by automated download); the volume was obtained instead from the Internet Archive copy of SIL's archive PDF.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Muinane has two contrastive tones, high and low, on every phonemic syllable (each vowel is a tone-bearing unit); the chapter has no notion of word stress at all — 'stress', 'accent' and 'prominence' do not occur anywhere in the 19 scanned pages. Attested word patterns: two-syllable words in isolation are only HL; three-syllable words HLH, LHL, HHL, LLH.
new_statements.exceptions: Allotones: low is raised after high, high lowered after low (§5.2); the pitch register of a whole pause group is higher when its initial syllable contains a front vowel (two levels realised as high/mid-low) than when it contains a central or back vowel (mid-high/low). The tone system is explicitly called not yet fully analysed.

new_statements.quote: p. 202: "Hay dos tonos fonemáticos en el muinane: alto y bajo. El tono no se puede predecir a base de la fonología, pero sí a base de la morfología. [...] Básicamente, el tono alto de la raíz se extiende hacia la derecha, dando a cada vocal un tono alto, hasta la última vocal antes de un sufijo que no puede llevarlo. De allí a la derecha, el tono de la palabra es bajo, no importa si los demás sufijos admiten tono alto o no. Hay algunas excepciones a esta regla. Primero, la última vocal de una palabra siempre lleva tono bajo, aunque sea un sufijo que admite tono alto." p. 1: "En este diccionario el tono alto se indica por medio de un acento agudo, tal como se marca el acento en español."
new_statements.translation: p. 202: "There are two phonemic tones in Muinane: high and low. Tone cannot be predicted from the phonology, but it can from the morphology. [...] Basically, the high tone of the root spreads to the right, giving each vowel a high tone, up to the last vowel before a suffix that cannot carry it. From there rightward the tone of the word is low, regardless of whether the remaining suffixes admit high tone or not. There are some exceptions to this rule. First, the last vowel of a word always carries low tone, even if it is a suffix that admits high tone." p. 1: "In this dictionary high tone is indicated by an acute accent, just as the accent is marked in Spanish."

new_statements.rule_in_words: Two lexical tones (H/L); the acute accent in the dictionary marks high tone, not stress (many words carry several). Tone is morphologically governed: the root's H spreads rightward through suffixes that can bear H until a suffix that cannot; everything after it is L; the word-final vowel is always L. Nothing on stress or accent as prominence.
new_statements.exceptions: Word-final vowel always low; in noun compounds the second root is always low; the suffixes -tɨ 'negative' and -ri 'con' block all rightward spreading, leaving H only on the first root syllable (or on prefixes); prefix tone spreads like root tone. The introduction notes that tone had not been marked in the practical orthography up to 1997 and is marked here experimentally.

tone_statements.citation: De Vengoechea, Consuelo (2026). Fonología del muinane en perspectiva comparada Noroeste amazónico [Muinane Phonology in a Comparative Perspective, Northwest Amazonia]. Lenguaje (Universidad del Valle, Cali) 54(1), e20413067. DOI 10.25100/lenguaje.v54i1.13067
tone_statements.quote: El sistema tonal combina tres posibilidades: tono alto, tono bajo y ausencia de tono (A, B, Ø). Las operaciones morfológicas o morfosintácticas producen con frecuencia cambios tonales. El alargamiento vocálico funciona de manera contrastiva a nivel del léxico, pero también puede ser resultado de operaciones morfológicas. La duración es representada por moras. La mora es la unidad que porta el tono. [...] Recordemos que a final de palabra no hay distinción tonal, pues siempre será realizada como un tono medio o bajo.
tone_statements.translation: The tonal system combines three possibilities: high tone, low tone and absence of tone (H, L, Ø). Morphological or morphosyntactic operations frequently produce tonal changes. Vowel lengthening is contrastive in the lexicon but can also result from morphological operations. Length is represented by morae. The mora is the tone-bearing unit. [...] Recall that word-finally there is no tonal distinction, since it is always realised as a mid or low tone.
tone_statements.locator: section 'Los rasgos y la prosodia del sistema muinane' > 'Propuesta fonológica' (first two paragraphs) and section on the phonological word ('La palabra en la lengua muinane..'); see also 'El sistema tonal' + Tabla 3 (JATS XML galley, unpaginated e-article)
tone_statements.summary: 2 level tones H/L plus toneless Ø (privative system); TBU = mora; nouns lexically H-specified, verbs get grammatical tone; word-final syllable neutralised (mid/low); tone changes under morphology; no stress statement.

readall_conflicts: No source disagrees about stress: none of the four distinct works (1967 phonemic statement, 1975 grammar, 1977 discourse article, 1997 dictionary) mentions word stress, accent or prominence at all, and the three that touch phonology all state a two-tone (high/low) system. The only tension is inside the tone description, not about stress: Walton & Walton 1967 (p. 43) list three-syllable patterns ending in high, e.g. 'high low high: dámé "leaf", nití?í "to wash"', while the 1997 dictionary appendix (p. 202) states that the last vowel of a word always carries low tone and that tone is predictable from morphology; the 1967 chapter itself calls its tone analysis 'not yet fully analyzed', so the 1997 rule reads as a later refinement rather than a contradiction.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: every fragment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the HAL thesis text we hold at the stated sections/pages (4.2 p.51; 4.4.1 p.78; (39) p.81; 4.4.4.5 p.97). Deciding source is a 2012 doctoral thesis with a full autosegmental phonology chapter by the language's principal phonologist; Glottolog lists nothing newer or more detailed on prosody, and web search found no instrumental or later phonological study. I downloaded and scanned-read the two independent SIL descriptions (Walton & Walton 1967, sect. 5, pp. 42-43; Walton, Hensarling & Maxwell 2000, sect. 9.1.3-9.1.4, p. 257): both posit exactly two tone phonemes (high/low) with the syllable as unit of tone placement and mention no stress or accent. Walton 1967 notes restricted word-tone patterns (disyllables only HL), which is consistent with Vengoechea's word-level tonal constraints (final mora toneless, no initial low sequence)

sources.citation: De Vengoechea, Consuelo (2026). Fonología del muinane en perspectiva comparada Noroeste amazónico [Muinane Phonology in a Comparative Perspective, Northwest Amazonia]. Lenguaje (Universidad del Valle, Cali) 54(1), e20413067. DOI 10.25100/lenguaje.v54i1.13067
sources.quote: El sistema tonal combina tres posibilidades: tono alto, tono bajo y ausencia de tono (A, B, Ø). Las operaciones morfológicas o morfosintácticas producen con frecuencia cambios tonales. El alargamiento vocálico funciona de manera contrastiva a nivel del léxico, pero también puede ser resultado de operaciones morfológicas. La duración es representada por moras. La mora es la unidad que porta el tono. [...] Recordemos que a final de palabra no hay distinción tonal, pues siempre será realizada como un tono medio o bajo.
sources.locator: section 'Los rasgos y la prosodia del sistema muinane' > 'Propuesta fonológica' (first two paragraphs) and section on the phonological word ('La palabra en la lengua muinane..'); see also 'El sistema tonal' + Tabla 3 (JATS XML galley, unpaginated e-article)
sources.note: Section 'El sistema tonal' + Tabla 3 'Sistemas tonales lenguas familia bora' and 'Propuesta fonológica': Muinane has H (A), L (B) and toneless Ø; nominal lexemes and a few grammatical morphemes lexically specified (H), verbs take grammatical tone schemes; mora = TBU; length contrastive; word-final position has no tonal contrast (realised mid or low); morphological operations frequently change tone; tone used in deverbal derivation and relative clauses; tonal spreading treated as a prosodic process in the feature-geometry model.

tone.translation: The tonal system combines three possibilities: high tone, low tone and absence of tone (H, L, Ø). Morphological or morphosyntactic operations frequently produce tonal changes. Vowel lengthening is contrastive in the lexicon but can also result from morphological operations. Length is represented by morae. The mora is the tone-bearing unit. [...] Recall that word-finally there is no tonal distinction, since it is always realised as a mid or low tone.
tone.summary: 2 level tones H/L plus toneless Ø (privative system); TBU = mora; nouns lexically H-specified, verbs get grammatical tone; word-final syllable neutralised (mid/low); tone changes under morphology; no stress statement.

sources.note: Reconstructs 416 proto Bora-Muinane word forms and 'the proto Bora-Muinane phonological system' and establishes sound changes in Bora and Muinane; both daughters are two-tone languages, so a statement of the Muinane tone system and tonal correspondences is likely; contents unseen.
